text:
This looks like mid-2008. Headline CPI is 4.0% YoY, the fed funds rate is 2.21% (it was 2.0% after April 2008), and payrolls are negative. Unemployment is 5.1%, which fits May 2008 (5.5% in June, 5.0% in April, 5.5% in May). The dollar is down 8.9% YoY. The Baa spread is 3.11 pp.

Headline CPI of 4.0% fits May 2008 (4.2%) or April 2008 (3.9%). The 10-year yield is 3.85% and the 2-year is 2.35%; in June 2008 the 2-year was about 2.9% and the 10-year about 4.0%, so this is probably earlier. The 3m change in the policy rate is -1.01, and the rate was 3.0% in January, so April is plausible. The effective rate was 2.0% in April and 1.9% in May, so 2.21 fits an April average (about 2.0)... or possibly March (2.2). March 2008 CPI was 4.0%, the 2-year about 1.6% and the 10-year about 3.5%, so that is not a clean match.

Taking April 2008: the 10-year was around 3.7–3.9% and the 2-year about 2.3–2.4%, and payrolls were negative. Equities show a 6m return of -9.4%, with a 1m gain of +1.2% and a 3m gain of +3.0%, which fits April. The 12m drawdown of -10.7% fits too. Unemployment of 5.1% is close to April's 5.0%.

The 3m change in the 10-year yield is +0.18, which suggests the 10-year was 3.67% in January, and that fits April.

I'll go with April 2008.
